newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST-Singapore Aug exports down 0.8 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Singapore Aug exports down 0.8 pct - poll.

text.p: The worldwide slowdown in the electronics and computer industries is continuing to hit Singapore's exports, a Reuters poll of economists suggested on Wednesday.
Eight leading financial institutions produced an average forecast of a fall of 0.8 percent year-on-year in nominal terms in Singapore's non-oil domestic exports in August.
This compares with a rise of 6.4 percent in July, a fall of 6.1 percent in June and fairly consistent double-digit export growth through last year and the early part of 1996.
Forecasts for August exports were spread over a wide range, from a slump of 4.5 percent to a rise of 3.5 percent.
All those polled blamed the current poor export performance on the drop in orders in the electronics industry, particularly in the United States.
Electronics and related products account for almost half Singapore's total industrial output and about 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
The same poll predicted an average rise of 1.5 percent year-on-year in Singapore's consumer price index (CPI) of inflation. The CPI rose 1.2 percent year-on-year in June.
Polling was carried out on September 17.
The Singapore government is expected to release its official August figures for trade on September 20. The August inflation data is expected to be published on September 23.
